answer: A procurement registry reserves collateral for every active supplier identity: 10 credits for vine cuttings, 20 for umber pigment and 30 for ferrous scrap. A verifier checks the declared goods class and an escrow locked to that key for 30 days; the same funds cannot back two registrations. Ten scrap suppliers therefore tie up 300 credits, even if one operator controls them all. Withdrawal disables bidding until a new lock matures. This imposes capital cost per alias, but wealthy operators can still buy many slots.
